# fortiappseccloud_waf_web_socket_security

Configures WebSocket security for one FortiAppSec Cloud application using the static app endpoint `/waf/apps/{ep_id}/web_socket_security`. Set `template = false` and provide `configs` to manage settings directly. Set `template = true` and omit `configs` to inherit this module from the application's attached WAF template.

Declare only one `fortiappseccloud_waf_web_socket_security` resource for an application endpoint. Template-level settings are managed by `fortiappseccloud_waf_template_web_socket_security`.

## Example Usage

```hcl
resource "fortiappseccloud_waf_web_socket_security" "example" {
  ep_id    = fortiappseccloud_waf_app.example.ep_id
  template = false

  configs {
    status = true
    action = "alert_deny"

    rule_list {
      item {
        name              = "ws-rule"
        url               = "/ws"
        allow_binary_text = true
        allow_plain_text  = true
        allow_websocket   = true
        block_attacks     = true
        block_extensions  = false
        max_frm_size      = 64
        max_msg_size      = 1024

        origin_list {
          item {
            origin = "https://example.com"
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

- `ep_id` (Required, Forces replacement) — Application endpoint ID. Import uses this exact value and it must contain a non-whitespace character.
- `template` (Required) — Whether effective configuration is inherited from the attached template.
- `configs` (Block) — Required when `template = false` and forbidden when `template = true`. State keeps this block null when template inheritance is enabled.
  - `action` (Optional, Computed) — Sets Action. One of `alert`, `alert_deny`, `deny_no_log`. Omission preserves the current value.
  - `status` (Optional, Computed) — Enables or disables WebSocket security. Omission preserves the current value.
  - Collection ownership — Each block below contains ordered `item` blocks. Omitting a collection block preserves the complete raw remote array and keeps the block null in state. A present empty block sends `[]`. A present block with items replaces the complete array in Terraform order.
    - `rule_list` (Optional Block, at most 12 items) — Owns the ordered `rule_list.item` blocks.
      - `rule_list.item.allow_binary_text` (Required) — Allow binary text.
      - `rule_list.item.allow_plain_text` (Required) — Allow plain text.
      - `rule_list.item.allow_websocket` (Required) — Allow websocket.
      - `rule_list.item.block_attacks` (Required) — Block attacks.
      - `rule_list.item.block_extensions` (Required) — Block extensions.
      - `rule_list.item.max_frm_size` (Required, between 0 and 2147483647) — Max frm size.
      - `rule_list.item.max_msg_size` (Required, between 0 and 2147483647) — Max msg size.
      - `rule_list.item.name` (Required, maximum 39 UTF-8 characters) — Rule name.
      - `rule_list.item.origin_list` (Optional Block, at most 256 items) — Ownership wrapper for ordered `rule_list.item.origin_list.item` blocks. Omitting the wrapper preserves the prior GET value opaquely (the provider merges the fresh GET's nested array into the outgoing item) and keeps the wrapper null in state; a present empty wrapper sends []; a present populated wrapper replaces the complete array.
        - `rule_list.item.origin_list.item.origin` (Optional, Computed, maximum 255 UTF-8 characters) — Origin.
      - `rule_list.item.url` (Required, maximum 255 UTF-8 characters, matching `^/.*$`) — Request URL.

The wire-only `idx` field is never exposed. The provider regenerates sequential one-based indices independently for each list, validates imported or owned response indices, and sorts state by `idx`. Unknown nested item keys fail closed for owned and imported arrays; omitted top-level collection wrappers remain opaque and are preserved unchanged. Nested sub-item array wrappers, when omitted, preserve the prior GET value opaquely and keep the wrapper null in state.


## Import

Import using the application `ep_id`:

```shell
terraform import fortiappseccloud_waf_web_socket_security.example application-endpoint-id
```

The first read after import hydrates all ownership wrappers when `template = false`.

## Destroy Behavior
Destroy performs a fresh GET, preserves the complete response, sets `template=false` and `configs.status=false`, sends the complete PUT, and verifies the normalized GET response before Terraform removes the resource from state.
